stories.title: Upgrade ESLint to v9 with flat config format
stories.description: ESLint v8 reached end-of-life in October 2024 and no longer receives security patches. Next.js 15 added first-class ESLint 9 support with the new flat config format (eslint.config.mjs), replacing .eslintrc* files. Migrating ensures continued security coverage and unlocks the new plugin ecosystem.
acceptanceCriteria: eslint upgraded to ^9.x in package.json devDependencies
Legacy .eslintrc.* replaced with eslint.config.mjs using flat config format
next/core-web-vitals and @typescript-eslint rules configured in flat config
`npm run lint` passes with zero errors and zero deprecation warnings
CI build log shows no ESLint 8 EOL warnings
technicalNotes: Run `npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest` — it handles eslint config migration automatically
Next.js 15 ships eslint-config-next compatible with ESLint 9 flat config
Flat config requires ESM import syntax; check all custom plugins for ESLint 9 compatibility
ESLint 8 EOL announcement: https://eslint.org/blog/2024/10/eslint-v8-end-of-life/

stories.title: Upgrade Tailwind CSS from v3 to v4
stories.description: Tailwind CSS v4 introduces a CSS-first configuration model, built-in cascade layers, and up to 5x faster full builds (100x faster incremental). The new engine eliminates tailwind.config.ts for most setups, using a @theme block in globals.css. This reduces configuration debt and improves HMR performance during development.
acceptanceCriteria: tailwindcss upgraded to ^4.x with @tailwindcss/postcss plugin
tailwind.config.ts content migrated to CSS @theme block in globals.css
@tailwindcss/typography upgraded to v4-compatible version
All existing Tailwind classes render correctly across all pages
Build time measured and confirmed to improve vs v3 baseline
technicalNotes: Run `npx @tailwindcss/upgrade` for automated config and class-rename migration
PostCSS config changes: replace `tailwindcss` plugin with `@tailwindcss/postcss`
Breaking: some utility names renamed (e.g., shadow-sm → shadow-xs); codemod handles most
Tailwind v4 upgrade guide: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide

stories.title: Audit and configure explicit cache policies for all Next.js 15 fetch calls
stories.description: Next.js 15 reversed its caching defaults: fetch() requests and GET Route Handlers are now uncached by default (breaking from v14). Any data fetching relying on implicit caching now returns fresh data every request, risking performance regressions. An explicit annotation pass ensures static pages are cached and dynamic pages are correctly tagged.
acceptanceCriteria: All server component fetch() calls have explicit { cache: 'force-cache' } or { next: { revalidate: N } }
Booking availability and pricing endpoints use { cache: 'no-store' }
Blog and guide pages use { next: { revalidate: 3600 } } for ISR
Static pages (about, amenities, rooms) export `const dynamic = 'force-static'`
No unexpected cache misses or stale data in booking flow after audit
technicalNotes: Next.js 15 caching change: https://nextjs.org/blog/next-15#caching-semantics
Set staleTimes in next.config.ts for Client Router Cache control
Use `export const revalidate = 86400` at segment level for semi-static pages
Verify with Chrome DevTools Network tab: static pages should return from cache on repeat visit

stories.title: Add Table of Contents component for blog posts and /guide long-form content
stories.description: Long-form pages (/guide and blog articles) lack navigational structure, forcing users to scroll linearly through content. A sticky Table of Contents with anchor links improves dwell time, satisfies WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks), and creates crawlable deep-links that trigger Google's 'jump to' snippets in search results.
acceptanceCriteria: TableOfContents component extracts H2/H3 headings and renders them as an anchor-linked list
Clicking a ToC entry smoothly scrolls to the heading with offset for sticky header height
Active heading is highlighted in ToC as user scrolls (Intersection Observer API)
ToC is sticky sidebar on desktop (lg:sticky) and collapsible accordion on mobile
All heading IDs are slug-formatted (kebab-case) for clean anchor URLs
Accessible: ToC nav has aria-label='Article table of contents'
technicalNotes: Extract heading data from blog post TypeScript data object at build time, not from DOM
Use Intersection Observer with rootMargin: '-20% 0% -70% 0%' to track active section
Apply scroll-margin-top equal to header height (64px) on all h2/h3 elements via globals.css
Google uses heading anchor links as 'jump to' suggestions in featured snippets

stories.title: Add estimated reading time to blog post cards and article headers
stories.description: Blog cards and article pages show no reading time, giving users no expectation of content length. Industry research shows reading time labels reduce bounce rate by setting expectations. The calculation (word count ÷ 200 wpm) can be computed at build time from static post body data with zero runtime cost.
acceptanceCriteria: Reading time displayed on BlogCard component (e.g., '5 min read')
Reading time displayed in blog article page header below the title
Calculated using Math.ceil(wordCount / 200) — minimum 1 min displayed
readingTimeMinutes field added to blog post TypeScript data type
Display uses an accessible pattern: 5 min read
technicalNotes: Add computeReadingTime(text: string): number utility function to data layer
Store pre-computed value in post data object to avoid runtime recalculation
Average adult reading speed: 200-238 wpm per scientific literature (JSTOR study)
Medium.com uses ~265 wpm; 200 wpm is conservative and appropriate for travel content

stories.title: Add Web Share API native share button to blog post pages
stories.description: Blog posts have no sharing mechanism. The Web Share API enables users to share content to WhatsApp, Telegram, email, or any installed app via the native OS share sheet on mobile. This is the highest-conversion sharing pattern for mobile users (no extra app installs, no redirect). A clipboard copy fallback handles unsupported desktop browsers.
acceptanceCriteria: Share button rendered on each blog post page with accessible label 'Share this article'
Clicking triggers navigator.share({ title, text, url }) on supported browsers
Clipboard copy fallback displayed for browsers without navigator.share support
Success toast notification shown after share or copy completes
Button requires user gesture (click) — no auto-share on load
navigator.canShare() checked before calling navigator.share()
technicalNotes: Add 'use client' directive — Web Share API requires browser context
Web Share API requires HTTPS (works on localhost for development)
Browser support: Chrome 89+, Safari 14+, Firefox Android 71+ — desktop Firefox does not support
MDN Web Share API: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/share

stories.title: Add Fuse.js client-side site search for blog and guide content
stories.description: With 6+ blog articles and a comprehensive guide page, users cannot quickly find specific topics, destinations, or tips. Fuse.js provides fast fuzzy search running entirely in the browser from a pre-built static index — no backend, no API costs, no privacy concerns. A keyboard-accessible Command Menu (Cmd/Ctrl+K) is the standard pattern for modern site search.
acceptanceCriteria: Search dialog opens via Cmd/Ctrl+K keyboard shortcut and a search icon in Header nav
Results include blog posts and /guide section headings with category labels
Fuzzy matching handles 1-2 character typos (e.g., 'restrant' finds 'restaurant')
Keyboard navigation works: arrow keys to move, Enter to navigate, Escape to close
Search index pre-built at build time from static data — zero runtime fetch required
Empty state message shown when no results match
Search dialog has role='dialog', aria-label='Site search', and focus trap
technicalNotes: npm install fuse.js (3.2 KB gzipped)
Fuse.js documentation: https://www.fusejs.io/
Use next/dynamic with ssr: false and loading='lazy' to keep Fuse.js out of initial bundle
Index fields and weights: title (3), tags (2), excerpt (1)
Pre-build index: export const searchIndex = buildIndex(blogPosts, guideSections)

This cross-platform entity linking strengthens local SEO authority and may trigger or improve the Knowledge Panel in branded searches.

sameAs array includes live TripAdvisor property URL

stories.description: The /guide page has TouristAttraction schema for individual JB landmarks but lacks a TouristDestination schema marking JB itself as the destination. schema.org TouristDestination (distinct from TouristAttraction) enables Google to categorise the page as a destination guide, linking it to the 'Things to Do' carousel and travel intent queries. stories.title: Implement dark mode support with prefers-color-scheme and Tailwind dark: classes
stories.description: Approximately 65% of mobile users enable dark mode at the OS level. The site has no dark mode support, causing bright white pages for night-time booking — a common scenario for late travellers. Tailwind's dark: variant (media strategy) provides automatic OS-preference matching with no JavaScript state management required.
acceptanceCriteria: tailwind.config.ts sets darkMode: 'media'
All page backgrounds switch to dark equivalents (dark:bg-stone-900 etc.) in dark mode
Header, Footer, Hero, Rooms, and all card components have dark: variants for text, borders, and backgrounds
No white flash on page load in dark mode (background-color set in globals.css body rule)
prefers-color-scheme: dark tested via Chrome DevTools Rendering panel
All text in dark mode passes WCAG 1.4.3 4.5:1 contrast ratio
technicalNotes: Start with darkMode: 'media' strategy — requires no toggle state management
Add dark background to body in globals.css: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { body { background-color: #1c1917; } }
Test with Chrome DevTools: Rendering > Emulate CSS media > prefers-color-scheme: dark
Images with white backgrounds: add dark:bg-stone-800 to containing divs or use transparent PNGs
Tailwind dark mode docs: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/dark-mode

stories.title: Add theme-color meta tags for browser UI colour in light and dark mode
stories.description: The site's manifest.ts exists but layout.tsx is missing <meta name='theme-color'> tags. These control the mobile browser toolbar and address bar colour in Chrome Android and Safari iOS 15+, creating a more native PWA-like experience. Separate light/dark values via the media attribute ensure the toolbar matches the page background in each colour scheme.
acceptanceCriteria: layout.tsx metadata includes themeColor with two entries: light (#fafaf9) and dark (#1c1917)
Using Next.js metadata API array form: themeColor: [{ color: '#fafaf9', media: '(prefers-color-scheme: light)' }, { color: '#1c1917', media: '(prefers-color-scheme: dark)' }]
manifest.ts theme_color updated to match the light theme-color value
Chrome Android toolbar colour verified to match page background via DevTools mobile emulation
No duplicate theme-color meta tags in rendered HTML
technicalNotes: MDN theme-color: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta/name/theme-color
Next.js metadata themeColor API: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#themecolor
Safari iOS uses apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style — add 'black-translucent' for dark mode
Verify in Chrome DevTools: Application > Manifest > Theme color

stories.title: Add contact inquiry form with Resend email auto-reply on /contact page
stories.description: The /contact page currently renders only a Location map component with no inquiry form. Potential guests must manually compose WhatsApp or email messages, increasing friction and drop-off. A structured form with check-in/out dates, number of guests, and message, plus an automated acknowledgment email via Resend, reduces friction and reassures guests their inquiry was received.

Client-side validation with accessible error messages on all required fields
Server Action sends inquiry details to hostel admin email on submission
Acknowledgment email auto-sent to guest confirming receipt within 2 seconds
Auto-reply includes: hostel name, direct booking link, WhatsApp number, expected response time (24h)
Honeypot hidden field rejects bot submissions server-side

Resend Next.js guide: https://resend.com/docs/send-with-nextjs
Use Next.js Server Actions for form handling — no separate API route needed
Store RESEND_API_KEY and ADMIN_EMAIL as environment variables
Resend free tier: 3,000 emails/month (sufficient for hostel volume)
Log submissions to avoid losing inquiries if email delivery fails

stories.title: Integrate Microsoft Clarity for heatmap and session recording analytics
stories.description: The site has GA4 page-view metrics but no behavioural analytics (heatmaps, scroll depth, session recordings). Microsoft Clarity is a free tool revealing where guests drop off in the booking funnel, which CTAs are ignored, and how far users scroll. Add to AnalyticsProvider.tsx or create a separate ClarityProvider component
Clarity snippet: (function(c,l,a,r,i,t,y){ c[a]=c[a]||function(){...} })('clarity','script','CLARITY_PROJECT_ID',...)

Free tier: unlimited sessions, unlimited recordings, 12-month data retention

stories.title: Add <link rel='preload'> for LCP hero image in layout <head>
stories.description: The hero image is the LCP element and determines Core Web Vitals scores. While next/image priority=true sets fetchpriority='high' at render time, adding an explicit <link rel='preload'> in the document <head> triggers browser preloading before React hydrates, potentially improving LCP by 200-500ms on slow connections by starting the download earlier in the network waterfall.
acceptanceCriteria: <link rel='preload' as='image' href='/images/hero-main.webp' type='image/webp'> added to layout.tsx <head>
imageSrcSet attribute on preload link matches Next.js Image srcset breakpoints
imageSizes='100vw' matches hero image usage
Chrome DevTools Network tab shows hero image download starting in first 1-2 waterfall requests
Lighthouse 'Preload Largest Contentful Paint image' opportunity resolves
No Chrome DevTools 'preload used within a few seconds of window load' warning
technicalNotes: Add preload link directly in layout.tsx <head> — Next.js metadata API does not support image preload links
Match srcSet breakpoints from Next.js image config: '640w, 750w, 828w, 1080w, 1200w, 1920w'
web.dev preload responsive images: https://web.dev/articles/preload-responsive-images
Ensure the hero-main.webp file exists in /public/images/ and the path matches exactly
Test: Lighthouse > Opportunities > 'Preload Largest Contentful Paint image' should disappear

stories.title: Add Bing Webmaster Tools verification and sitemap submission

Verification takes under 5 minutes, enables sitemap submission, crawl monitoring, and Bing-specific SEO insights. Bing also powers DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, and Yahoo Search — one submission covers all.

Bing can auto-import verified GSC sites — check for auto-import option first to save time

stories.title: Add OpenSearch XML descriptor for browser address bar site search
stories.description: Firefox and Chrome support OpenSearch 1.1, allowing users to add a site's search as a browser search engine after visiting a page with a valid opensearch.xml descriptor. This provides a low-friction re-engagement path: returning guests can search the hostel site directly from the browser address bar without navigating to the homepage first.

stories.title: Add schema.org Offer markup for hostel room rates on /rooms page
stories.description: The /rooms page displays room types and pricing but has no Offer schema markup. Adding schema.org Offer (with price, priceCurrency, and availability) on each room type enables Google to display pricing rich results (e.g., 'From RM35/night') in search snippets. The HotelRoom > makesOffer > Offer pattern is the recommended combination per Google's hotel structured data guide.

AggregateOffer added to LodgingBusiness schema with lowPrice: '35', highPrice: '55', priceCurrency: 'MYR'
Offer.seller references the hostel LodgingBusiness @id

Pattern: HotelRoom > makesOffer > Offer — see existing HotelRoom schema in /rooms page

stories.title: Migrate CSP script-src from unsafe-inline to nonce-based policy
stories.description: The current CSP in next.config.ts uses 'unsafe-inline' in script-src (line 7), which allows any inline script to execute regardless of origin — significantly weakening XSS protection. A nonce-based CSP generates a cryptographic nonce per request, allowing only explicitly nonced inline scripts (Next.js hydration, analytics) while blocking unauthorised injected scripts.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-request cryptographic nonce generated in Next.js middleware and passed via x-nonce request header
'unsafe-inline' removed from script-src; nonce added: "'nonce-{VALUE}'"
Next.js layout.tsx reads nonce from headers() and applies it to inline script tags
Sentry inline scripts receive the nonce attribute via Sentry's nonce configuration option
GA4 / @next/third-parties scripts receive the nonce
No CSP violation errors in browser console on any page after migration
Mozilla Observatory score improves to A or higher for script-src policy
technicalNotes: Next.js nonce-based CSP guide: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/configuring/content-security-policy
Generate nonce: Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64') in middleware.ts
Set nonce in middleware: requestHeaders.set('x-nonce', nonce)
Read in layout.tsx server component: const nonce = (await headers()).get('x-nonce') ?? ''
Add 'strict-dynamic' to allow dynamically-loaded trusted scripts alongside nonce
Test with: https://csp-evaluator.withgoogle.com/

One-line addition to hostelSchema object in site/src/components/StructuredData.tsx
